text.en: Red cells carry oxygen and white cells guard the body.

The aim is to identify red and white blood cells from permanent slides, draw labelled diagrams and write notes.
Red blood cells (erythrocytes) are biconcave discs; mature mammalian RBCs have no nucleus and contain haemoglobin, which gives the red colour and transports oxygen and carbon dioxide.
White blood cells (leucocytes) are colourless and have a nucleus. They defend the body against germs. Draw both types with labels.
